arch.title: Solution and network architecture
principles: Our collector reads the vendor's existing OPC UA server from outside. No host is added to their network, no software installed on their machines, no change to their topology.
Everything we run sits between two firewalls
The collector, historian and jump host live in an industrial DMZ; the APC engine in a zone of its own. Each is reachable only through a boundary that inspects and logs.
No session crosses from end to end
OPC UA stops at the collector and MQTT starts there, so what reaches the cloud is a new conversation carrying only the values we chose to publish. Nothing from the north side can reach a controller.
One component can write, and it is bounded
The APC holds a dedicated account scoped to its own tags, has no route north at all, and writes setpoints the controller clamps for rate and range.
legend: remote access — VPN in the IT network, then a second authentication at the jump host
the only flow that can change the process

estimation.title: Estimation layer — zone soot deposit
estimation.sub: Grey-box thermal model + Bayesian state estimation · plant-specific, learned from own history
steps: Per-zone thermal state-space model; states represent surface cleanliness. Deposit is unmeasurable, so it is treated as a hidden state observed through its thermal signature — exit-gas temperature rise and draft loss.
Model parameters learned once from the plant's own multi-month DCS history (EM-based system identification). No generic or third-party data; the model is specific to this boiler.

An Extended Kalman Filter fuses 15 live sensors — 7 zone flue-gas temperatures, ID-fan / furnace draft, steam temperature and flow, SB status flags — into a 0–100 % deposit estimate per zone, updated every 4 minutes.
Each of the 29 blowers inherits the deposit of the dirtiest zone it can physically reach, giving a directly rankable cleaning priority.
note: model structure, identified parameters, filter tuning and fouling-rate priors are Faclon proprietary and are not disclosed in plant documentation.

decision.title: Decision layer — constrained batch scheduler
decision.sub: Receding-horizon (MPC-style) optimisation: hold thermal and draft limits with the least soot-blowing steam
decision.objective: Minimise SB steam use subject to zone thermal limits, draft limits and rotation coverage — re-solved every cycle on the latest deposit estimates. Blows in batches ~every 2 h; no fixed timers.
constraints: Batch size 8 (grows to 10 only on boiler-bank relief)
Daily cap 100 blows / operating day (corners exempt)
No-starve: any blower idle 3 batches is forced in
Priority cadence: 9 key BB/PSH lances ≥ once / 3 batches
Corner blowers first in every batch (draft relief)
overrides: Staged corner relief; escalate; alert if load-driven
Charge header only around blow window
note: ranking is re-optimised as deposits evolve, so steam goes where heat-transfer recovery per blow is highest — the source of the measured steam reduction.

safety.title: Safety interlocks & fail-safe design
safety.sub: All 9 checks must pass simultaneously before every blow — a blow is held, never forced
failsafe: Temperature / pressure gates require the last 5 readings to pass — never an average
Header is never depressurised with a lance extended; all-home confirmed first
Stale data (> 5 min) locks out both charging and blowing
ISB OFF at any time → batch stops safely, header closes, retry in 10 min
Every command re-issued until DCS confirms; a blow counts only when confirmed
Operator alerts: ISB off, blower on manual, pressure hold, header not charging, ID-fan high

validation.title: Validation basis & assumptions
blocks: SB steam integrated from DCS flow; a blow counts only on DCS confirmation. Base 95 t/day = last-year actual, and Aug'26 saving (₹13.3 L at ₹1,487/t) certified in SPB's monthly report. Aug adoption: 95 % of blows, 89 % of time in AI mode.
Before/after windows at same load profile; SGR computed as gross steam generated ÷ BLS fired over matched periods.
SB steam saving is consumption-side; SGR gain is generation-side. The two lines value different physical quantities.
Steam cost ₹1,487/t · power ₹6/kWh · 350 operating days · ECC TG: incremental SSC 5 kg/kWh through condensing tail (65 kg/cm² / 457 °C HP recovery boiler) · BLS 926 t/day derived, not metered.
Every ±₹1/kWh on power ≈ ±₹0.71 Cr/yr; every ±0.05 on ΔSGR ≈ ±₹1.94 Cr/yr; ±0.5 kg/kWh on SSC ≈ ∓₹0.43 Cr/yr. Steam held at certified 28.8 t/day.
